_comment: Which of eblume's repos the `agents` bot may touch, and which land in the
agent workspace's checkout pool. THE single source of truth for both halves:
access -> reconciled onto the forge as collaborator grants by
`mise run agent-repo-access` (.forgejo/workflows/agent-repo-access.yaml)
pool   -> compiled into the pod's clone loop by ./default.nix (fromJSON)
Before this file existed those were two independent steps and a missed grant
looked exactly like a typo (Forgejo 404s rather than 403s for a private repo
you cannot see), so timberborn-parsimony sat documented-but-absent for weeks.
access: write | read | none   (none = revoke any existing collaboration)
pool:   canonical | fork | none
canonical = clone eblume/<repo> directly (bot pushes branches there)
fork      = origin is agents/<repo>, upstream is eblume/<repo> read-only;
edits land via cross-repo PR (a human gate)
none      = access is granted, but no checkout in the pod
RECONCILE IS AUTHORITATIVE: a repo absent from this list has its `agents`
collaboration REMOVED. Adding a repo means adding it here, not clicking in
the forge UI. See docs/reference/infrastructure/agents-forgejo-bot.md.
`agents` and `blumeops` are pinned to read by an invariant in the reconciler
that this file cannot override -- their read-only-on-canonical status is what
keeps blumeops CI (and its deploy secrets) out of agent reach.
